thread:
Liam (AE): FYI MercuryTrust POC reported very slow TTFT for tiny prompts this morning (>20s). Also saw some 503s during peak. Can we triage + answer pricing + compliance?

Sana (SE): On it. Any sample req id or payload?

Liam (AE): req=a7c4f9 sample: `POST /v1/generate model=redwood-small prompt=\"Flag txn\" conv_id=random-uuid` They said many conv_ids are unique per request.

Evan (SRE): Pulling infra logs. Quick glance: org=mercurytrust prefix_cache_hit=7% batch_size=48 queue_wait=140ms gpu_load: 85/88. No big 429s but some 503s from gateway timeouts during spike.

Sana (SE): 7% cache hit is near-zero. If they rotate convo ids each time, KV cache can't help.

Noor (Solutions Eng): Recommend two paths: ask Mercury devs to reuse conversation ids where possible OR add a tiny session warmup (1-2 token) at session creation. Also can enable org-level persistent prefix cache on Dedicated or Hosted for enterprise customers.

Evan (SRE): Pasting log snippet around req a7c4f9:

```
[2026-04-02T14:02:11Z] req=a7c4f9 node=gw-3 batch=48 queue_wait=140ms kv_prefetch=false compile=fp16_v1 exec=19800ms
[2026-04-02T14:02:11Z] gpu0_load=84% gpu1_load=88% prefetched_prefix=null
```

Evan (SRE): The majority of the 20s is model exec + CPU prep when kv miss. Large batches of short requests are hurting TTFT.

Sana (SE): Client-side mitigation: limit parallel inflight per session (2-3), use streaming so UI shows partial tokens, and add jitter to avoid synchronized bursts.

Liam (AE): Mercury asked for Dedicated quote for mid-bank: 600 concurrent sessions, ~350k tokens/day. Also asked: do warmups count as billable tokens and what about HSM + SOC2?

Noor (Solutions Eng): Warmup calls are billed like normal tokens. For 1-token warmup per session x 600 sessions = negligible. HSM: we support customer-managed keys (HSM-backed via AWS CloudHSM or KMS with HSM). SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; we can provide ATO pack. Data residency: Dedicated/private deploy or regional hosting.

Liam (AE): Can we get a quick cost estimate + a one-pager for compliance to send to Mercury?

Noor (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a quote (cpu/gpu sizing + monthly commit + overage) and compliance blurb by EOD. Suggest Dedicated pool: 3x A10x4 equivalent for this profile.

Evan (SRE): Ops note: enabling org-prefix-cache requires infra toggle. I'm available to flip tonight at 02:00 UTC; zero-downtime. Will coordinate with deploy-bot.

Liam (AE): Perfect. Mercury wants the fastest path: try Hosted warmup + org cache before Dedicated. Is that doable?

Sana (SE): Yes. We can enable org-level prefix caching on Hosted temporarily and push a warmup shim in the SDK. I'll share curl + Node snippets now.

Sana (SE): curl example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-small\",\"prompt\":\"warmup\",\"org_id\":\"mercurytrust\",\"conversation_id\":\"<session>\"}'
```

Sana (SE): Node snippet:

```
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'warmup', org_id: 'mercurytrust', conversation_id: sessionId })
```

Noor (Solutions Eng): I'll include warmup cost calc in the quote: for 350k tokens/day, +600 warmups/day = trivial (<0.5%).

Liam (AE): Compliance-bot pinged for docs. compliance-bot: requested docs attached: SOC2 report link, KMS whitepaper, data-residency FAQs.

deploy-bot: scheduled: toggle-org-cache org=mercurytrust at 2026-04-03T02:00:00Z. Runbook: toggle -> validate cache hit metric -> rollback if error.

Evan (SRE): I'll execute change and monitor. Please have Mercury run a warmup test after toggle.

Liam (AE): Will ask Mercury to run a morning QA test. Thanks team. We'll reconvene if TTFT not improved. :thumbsup:
